notes: MCP TOOLS that drive the tab the agent works in (ordinary browser automation: navigate, snapshot, click, type, scroll, screenshot, wait, crawl the UI). The crate skeleton exists (Cargo.toml, an empty lib.rs with `register`); fill it in. Read rever-tools-api/src/tool.rs and utils.rs first, then rever-tools-page/src/lib.rs and one of its tool files as the house pattern to copy (the `tool!` macro, `Args`, `validate`, `schema`, `done`, the fake `Browser` in tests) — copy those helpers into this crate rather than depending on rever-tools-page. Implement `Tool` for each tool: `def()` returns `ToolDef::new("<name>", "<description>", <schema>)` with the name as a string literal at that call, the description copied verbatim from the TypeScript because it is prompt text, and the schema being the zod schema converted to JSON Schema (same property names, types, enums, defaults, limits, descriptions, required list). lib.rs `register` registers them in the order the TypeScript does. Output text must equal the TypeScript's: same wording, same JSON shape and key order (serde_json preserve_order is on, keep it). Module state in the TypeScript goes in a struct fetched with `ctx.state::<T>()`. Page access is only through `ctx.browser` (the `Browser` trait in rever-tools-api/src/tool.rs: page, navigate, back, forward, reload, evaluate, screenshot, input, viewport, cookies, add_init_script). The accessibility snapshot and ref resolution are already ported in the rever-snapshot crate (`Snapshotter`: take_snapshot, point_for_ref, act_on_ref, focus_ref, select_ref, scroll_ref_by, `point_for_selector`): read rever-snapshot/src/lib.rs and snapshot.rs and reuse them, do not re-port snapshot logic. `src/main/mcp/cdp-eval.ts` maps to `Browser::evaluate`; `src/main/mcp/bridge.ts` and `src/main/mcp/human-input.ts` are helpers of the tools: port their logic that is independent of Chrome DevTools Protocol (pure functions, timing and path math, argument handling) and route the dispatch through `Browser::input` / `Browser::evaluate`. Where the TypeScript needs a Chrome DevTools Protocol call or Electron API with no `Browser` counterpart (native dialogs, file upload, tab list, modifier-key clicks if `Input` cannot express them, and so on), do NOT edit rever-tools-api or rever-snapshot: keep the tool registered with its full schema and validation, return an error built with `rever_tools_api::tool::unsupported("<what>")` from that path, and list the missing capability under behaviorDifferences in your report, naming the exact trait method that would be needed. Async: `call` returns a boxed future run on a tokio runtime; tests use #[tokio::test] and a fake `Browser` in the test module that records calls and returns canned JSON. A file gets the `Port of` marker only when it is ported completely (for a tool file: all of its tools registered); otherwise start it with `Partial port of ...` saying what is there and why the rest is not.
